Growth in what?

Beneath any notion of change (i.e., growth) is a construct that
is changing over time
Height and weight are common points of reference
Constructs in education are not manifest like physical
measurements
Need, at a minimum, an underlying semantical referent (e.g.
reading or math)

Growth using Performance Standards

Strengths
Anchors reference points for discussions about performance
Growth is embedded in accountability metric
Common core standards will give uniform meaning across
states (unlike today where standards vary greatly with
stringency)
Limitations
Few levels, mask substantial range within levels thus masking
student growth within level

Growth using Scale Scores

Strengths
Semi-continuous scores (many score points)
Can be used to create vertical scales across grade levels
Give the appearance of interval scales needed by some
analytical models
Limitations
Difficult to interpret or explain to users
Vertical scales are hard to defend
Claims of interval measurement properties don’t hold to close
scrutiny

Vertical Scales
Vertical & Interval scales required for some analytic
techniques:
Gain score calculation (magnitude of growth)
Growth curve analysis (rate of growth) (e.g., Singer & Willett,
Vertical & Interval scales required for some questions:
Matthew effects: Do higher achievers grow faster than lower
achievers?
Growth rates relative to student age: Do students grow more in
later grades than earlier grades?
Invariance to monotone transformation of scale
If a developmental/vertical scale exists for a sequence of
assessments, the existing scale is a monotone transformation
of that scale.
Growth analyses that are invariant to monotone transformation
of scale obviate the need for a vertical scale in many cases.

Career and College Readiness

Before: Reach/Maintain proficiency. Now: Reach
career/college readiness
Challenge for consortia is to combine norm- and
criterion-referenced growth.
Criteria combined with norms provide a transparent and fair
mechanism to communicate simultaneously:
What is?
What should be?
What is reasonable?
